}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET

ET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}
/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST
.../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if th
e window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `window
Id` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it

stays dismissed when insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `us
age` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` desc
ribe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `
staleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map inde
pendently. Reading this response never starts analysis.\n\nTaxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Them
e ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unch
anged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with versio
n provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.\n\nCheck `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
\nwhole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed
counts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather\nthan a fabricated map

node.

The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open objects** on purpose.
Their upstream projections grow with the
product and the SDK types them the\nsame way, so pinning a field list would turn every new metric into a spec\nviolation. Read wha

t you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.
\n> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers.
Poll the window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is\n> why it is never i

nferred from anything else.

**Feedback** — report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does
|\n| - | - |\n| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kin
d, summary, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored.
Signed-in accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validate
d strictly — an empty or over-long key is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text g

oes to the MCPJam team, outside your organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same e
ndpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one —\n> it
lets the team find that request in the server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true`

with the original
> receipt instead of filing a second report.

**Planning** — one read that answers "may I?" before you try

:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, the beta gate's st

ate, plan limits, and the booleans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write
still enforces\n> independently, so a `true` here that races a flag flip costs you a clean\n> `403` rather than an incorrect succ
ess — and nothing should consult it\n> *instead of* trying. It exists because agent surfaces are static: an MCP tool\n> catalog is
built with no organization in hand, so the alternative is\n> attempting the write and reading the failure, by which point the age

nt has
> usually already told someone what it was about to do.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](ht

## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-
in, for example because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nt

o a named account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `
GET .../accounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project
|\n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or
replaces its token in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDe

fault: true`), or both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

sh theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVE

\\n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformat

needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressin

g an account

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account
or answers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no a
ccount has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with bo

th ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64
characters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names

are
unique on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is y

our own label, and
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
* **Upload
ed accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the accoun
t's owner\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in
the project.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `o
authResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is
at most 16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run,
